title: Untitled (etching on cream paper, stormy sea)
service: Hugging Face Space Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo, anonymous Gradio API (no account)
prompt: Photograph of an unsigned, untitled original monochrome black ink etching on cream paper, completely blank paper margins with no writing, no pencil inscription, fine hatched lines, the print shows a stormy sea, far out in the sea the ruined West Pier, only a small collapsed blackened skeletal iron frame of a former domed concert hall, half its ribs missing, on a cluster of thin bent iron legs, no deck, no railings, an isolated island of rusted wreckage standing alone in the sea, completely disconnected from the shore, nobody on it, small and distant, gulls, a wooden groyne on the shingle in the foreground, museum photograph of the whole sheet
settings: resolution 1536x1024, seed 9311, 9 steps, shift 3.0; native output 1536x1024, stored as JPEG q92
terms_note: Model and Space are both Apache 2.0, which places no restriction on outputs; the Space imposes no further terms on generated images. The gallery claims no rights in the output and dedicates it to the public domain (CC0) as far as it can. Fabricated painting: nothing in it was ever painted, drawn or printed by hand.
note: The prompt was written by the curator, an AI; chosen from a batch of six on looks alone. Two earlier etchings were discarded (the ruin grew a long railed deck, and the margins filled with invented pencil inscriptions), as were a pinhole photograph that came out ordinarily sharp, a tintype with the rust hand-coloured in, and a view from a boat in which the ruin seemed to reach the beach. Two specks of faint scratched marks remain in the bottom margin, as on many real plates. The image is shown unedited apart from resizing for the web.
